definitions.explanation: A position with little real work or responsibility, often implying the person has been sidelined or demoted without being formally dismissed. Carries a negative connotation of being shelved.

examples.japanese: {閑職|かんしょく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{回|まわ}された→回す：01158_mawasu⟧。
examples.english: I was transferred to a dead-end position.

examples.japanese: ⟦{部長|ぶちょう}→部長：01017_buchou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{失敗|しっぱい}→失敗：01636_shippai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{責任|せきにん}→責任：03298_sekinin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{取|と}らされ、{閑職|かんしょく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{追|お}いやられた。
examples.english: The department head was held responsible for the failure and pushed into a dead-end position.

examples.japanese: ⟦{定年|ていねん}→定年：07500_teinen⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧{閑職|かんしょく}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{過|す}ごす→過ごす：02062_sugosu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{辛|つら}い→辛い：01112_tsurai⟧もの⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Spending the time until retirement in a do-nothing position is a painful experience.

notes:
USAGE:
{閑職|かんしょく} almost always carries a negative connotation. Being placed in a {閑職|かんしょく} is a form of indirect punishment or marginalization in Japanese corporate and government culture, where outright firing is uncommon.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {閑職|かんしょく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{回|まわ}される→回す：01158_mawasu⟧ (to be transferred to a dead-end post)
- {閑職|かんしょく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{追|お}いやられる (to be pushed into a sinecure)
- {閑職|かんしょく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{就|つ}く→就く：10123_tsuku⟧ (to be placed in a quiet position)
- {閑職|かんしょく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{甘|あま}んじる→甘んじる：26968_amanjiru⟧ (to resign oneself to a quiet post)
